players.product: The Generate Platform (machine-learning generative biology; computational design integrated with large-scale biological experimentation) and AI-engineered protein therapeutics such as GB-0895

quarterly_data.signal: Amgen and Novartis collaboration economics (President and CFO Jason Silvers): the collaborations, signed with Amgen at the end of 2021 and Novartis late in 2024, cover a select number of targets (a total of nine targets between the two); Generate generates molecules to lead-candidate or DC-nomination criteria, the partner verifies them and pays milestones, and may advance them into the clinic with further milestones and potential royalties. Milestones are in the mid to upper $300 million on each program, with royalties of mid-single digits up to low-double digits. Generate has received the first milestone on the first Amgen program and believes it will receive multiple milestones on both partnerships over the next 12 months-18 months; verification timing is the biggest impediment. Some targets will reach criteria but not advance where the biology does not work. Generate is nearing resolution on most, if not all, targets, opening capacity for more partnerships, which remain part of its core strategy.
quarterly_data.figure: nine targets; milestones mid to upper $300 million per program; royalties mid-single digits up to low-double digits; first Amgen milestone received; multiple milestones expected over the next 12-18 months

quarterly_data.signal: Novartis (collaboration partner), CEO Michael Nally: one task both Amgen and Novartis gave Generate, unsolved by them for almost a decade, was to stabilize a native hormone with a thousandfold improvement in selectivity; Generate gave Novartis 40 molecules with over a 10,000-fold improvement in selectivity in four months. The CFO says Novartis work has moved even faster than Amgen's because Generate had many more people and capabilities when that deal was signed.
quarterly_data.figure: 40 molecules with over 10,000-fold improvement in selectivity in four months

quarterly_data.signal: Platform evidence (CEO): with a good prior generative model Generate can change up to 70% of an antibody's binding region versus about 10% with error-prone PCR or Rosetta, which is how GB-0895 was designed; across the five programs that have entered the clinic the molecules have been very well behaved with very low ADA rates, which the CEO says de-risked immunogenicity for all of Generate's programs. The CEO calls Generate 'a platform with a pipeline' and says next-generation programs take on more complex biology such as pH-dependent binding and ultra-high selectivity, partly because China can now rapidly reach affinity-maturation answers like GB-0895's roughly 20-fold affinity improvement over Tezspire.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 70% of binding region changed (vs about 10% historically); very low ADA rates across five clinical programs

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 profile and newer ERS data (CEO, CFO): preclinically GB-0895 showed a five-time potency improvement over Tezspire, but at the 300 mg Phase 3 dose it saturates the target at 99.9%, similar to Tezspire's 210 mg approved dose, so the CFO says it is 'really a convenience play' rather than an efficacy play in trials; it has a 98-day half-life and 100 femtomolar binding (20-fold better affinity than tezepelumab). CEO: the ERS data show the biomarker reductions sustained out to about a year, with 50% reductions in EOS, IL-5 and IL-13 and substantial FeNO reductions and no waning at 300 mg, so 'the medicine is very active for beyond six months.' CFO: the 786-subject, two-study size follows FDA feedback to be powered for the below-300 EOS endpoint; he believes 'the probabilities of the phase III success are probably very, very high.'
quarterly_data.figure: five-time preclinical potency vs Tezspire; 99.9% target saturation at 300 mg; 98-day half-life; 100 femtomolar binding; biomarker reductions sustained to about a year

quarterly_data.signal: SOLAIRIA execution and bar (CEO views): the main risks he watches are geographically balanced enrollment (recent asthma trials in Eastern Europe have shown no placebo-versus-active difference), entry-criteria adjudication and stratification by EOS level (below 150, 150-300, 300 and greater). He puts the competitive bar at somewhere around a 50% exacerbation reduction across all comers, set by Tezspire (56% blended), with a strong safety profile. In COPD he notes Dupixent and Nucala are approved only in the above-300 EOS cohort (about 28% of the market), that reaching the 150 EOS cohort would add about 40%-45% of the market, that COPD is only 2%-3% penetrated by biologics, and that six-monthly dosing may be more valuable in the frailer COPD population.
quarterly_data.figure: competitive bar ~50% exacerbation reduction across all comers; COPD biologic penetration 2%-3%

quarterly_data.signal: GB-4362 (MMAE neutralizer) update (CFO, CEO): FDA feedback, under the Fast Track designation in first-line therapy, is that Generate can go up to 80% free-MMAE reduction, but it targets 50% to preserve the bystander effect. With the first dose-escalation cohort completed, Generate expects the 50%-reduction dose toward the beginning of 2027, then a cohort expansion of somewhere between 40 and 60 urothelial cancer subjects with Grade 1 peripheral neuropathy on PADCEV and KEYTRUDA, with safety and efficacy data over the course of 2027 that could support moving directly to registrational trials with a safety endpoint. The CEO says there is no formal relationship on PADCEV, the drug is layered on the U.S. first-line standard of care, development would likely extend to a basket trial across MMAE-based ADCs and possibly co-formulation, and Generate is not aware of anyone else pursuing the concept.
quarterly_data.figure: expansion cohort 40 to 60 subjects; 50% reduction dose toward the beginning of 2027; data over the course of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Policy views (CEO): uncertainty at the FDA 'has not helped anyone in the industry' given long-lead-time bets, and MFN pricing will be deflationary for the whole industry; drawing on six years leading parts of Merck's European business, he expects government price negotiation to become a recurring cost-savings lever rather than a one-time event.
